Under [Chapter VII](/wiki/Chapter_VII_of_the_United_Nations_Charter "Chapter VII of the United Nations Charter") of the UN Charter, the Council may identify threats to international peace, determine breaches of that peace, and authorize responses up to and including the [use of force](/wiki/Use_of_force_in_international_law "Use of force in international law"). It is the only UN body with the authority to issue [resolutions](/wiki/United_Nations_Security_Council_resolution "United Nations Security Council resolution") binding on all member states.[[2]](#cite_note-Article24-4) The Council also recommends the admission of new member states to the [UN General Assembly](/wiki/United_Nations_General_Assembly "United Nations General Assembly"),[[3]](#cite_note-5) and approves changes to the Charter.[[4]](#cite_note-6)

Average annual precipitation is 39.61 inches (1,006 mm) and precipitation is greatest in May while least in October; annual precipitation has historically ranged from 22.65 in (575 mm) in 1930 to 57.83 in (1,469 mm) in 2018.[[81]](#cite_note-83) On average, December and January have the greatest number of precipitation days. Her father acceded to the throne in 1936 upon [the abdication](/wiki/Abdication_of_Edward_VIII "Abdication of Edward VIII") of his brother [Edward VIII](/wiki/Edward_VIII "Edward VIII"), making the ten-year-old Princess Elizabeth the [heir presumptive](/wiki/Heir_presumptive "Heir presumptive"). She was educated privately at home and began to undertake public duties during the [Second World War](/wiki/Second_World_War "Second World War"), serving in the [Auxiliary Territorial Service](/wiki/Auxiliary_Territorial_Service "Auxiliary Territorial Service"). In November 1947, [she married](/wiki/Wedding_of_Princess_Elizabeth_and_Philip_Mountbatten "Wedding of Princess Elizabeth and Philip Mountbatten") [Philip Mountbatten](/wiki/Philip_Mountbatten "Philip Mountbatten"), a former [prince of Greece and Denmark](/wiki/Prince_of_Greece_and_Denmark "Prince of Greece and Denmark"). Their marriage lasted 73 years until [his death in 2021](/wiki/Death_and_funeral_of_Prince_Philip,_Duke_of_Edinburgh "Death and funeral of Prince Philip, Duke of Edinburgh"). In the case of birds, storms may overcome a flock in flight, especially in times of migration. The Doppler image to the right shows an example wherein a group of bats is overtaken by a thunderstorm.[[16]](#cite_note-16) In the image, the bats are in the red zone, which corresponds to winds moving away from the radar station, and enter into a [mesocyclone](/wiki/Mesocyclone "Mesocyclone") associated with a tornado (in green). These events may occur easily with birds, which can get killed in flight, or stunned and then fall (unlike flightless creatures, which first have to be lifted into the air by an outside force). Sometimes this happens in large groups, for instance, the [blackbirds](/wiki/Red-winged_Blackbird "Red-winged Blackbird") falling from the sky in [Beebe, Arkansas](/wiki/Beebe,_Arkansas "Beebe, Arkansas"), United States, on 31 December 2010.[[17]](#cite_note-17) It is common for birds to become disoriented (for example, because of bad weather or fireworks) and collide with objects such as trees or buildings, killing them or stunning them into falling to their death. The number of blackbirds killed in Beebe is not spectacular considering the size of their congregations, which can be in the millions.[[18]](#cite_note-18) The event in Beebe, however, captured the imagination and led to more reports in the media of birds falling from the sky across the globe, such as in [Sweden](/wiki/Sweden "Sweden") and [Italy](/wiki/Italy "Italy"),[[19]](#cite_note-19) though many scientists claim such mass deaths are common occurrences but usually go unnoticed.[[20]](#cite_note-20) In contrast, it is harder to find a plausible explanation for rains of terrestrial animals.
